name: National Gallery - Alexandros Soutzos Museum
funding: Greek state museum. The ministry assured EUR 42M of the EUR 59M expansion (2021). The Stavros Niarchos Foundation gave EUR 13M in 2017.
watch: March 2025: MP Nikos Papadopoulos damaged four works he called blasphemous. September: 400 believers sought a court ban on the show; refused.
why_flagged: Greek state museum. The ministry assured EUR 42M of the EUR 59M expansion (2021). The Stavros Niarchos Foundation gave EUR 13M in 2017.
records_note: It posts no annual reports, accounts or sponsor list; its structure page names the board of directors, and its footer links to the Diavgeia register.

name: National Gallery
records_note: It posts annual reports and accounts from 2005 to 2025, names supporters by tier in its 2025 review, and lists its trustees.

name: National Gallery of Australia
funding: Commonwealth statutory body. 2024-25 major partners: Qantas Airways and Pallion; Wesfarmers Arts is First Nations Arts Partner. Mazda backed the 2024 Gauguin show.
why_flagged: Commonwealth statutory body. 2024-25 major partners: Qantas Airways and Pallion; Wesfarmers Arts is First Nations Arts Partner. Mazda backed the 2024 Gauguin show.
records_note: The gallery posts annual reports for 2022-23 to 2024-25 with audited accounts and Council names, plus an undated named partner list.

name: National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA)
funding: Government of India. A subordinate office of the Ministry of Culture, founded in 1954, with branches in Mumbai and Bengaluru.
watch: In 2000 the Culture Ministry ordered a painting pulled and all the artists withdrew. In 2019 members cut off Amol Palekar's criticism of the ministry.
why_flagged: Run as a subordinate office of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, since its 1954 opening, with centres in Mumbai and Bengaluru. No sponsor is listed.
records_note: It posts nothing itself; its parent Ministry of Culture publishes annual reports from 2014-15 to 2023-24, with no sponsor list or advisory board named.

name: National Gallery Prague
funding: State gallery supported by the Ministry of Culture, the Senate and the EU-funded National Recovery Plan. General partner Komerční banka; others include J&T Banka, Bohemia Sekt and Czech Television.
watch: A public call by artists and 23 advisory-board resignations in June 2024 criticised director Knastová. Minister Klempíř dismissed her on 19 March 2026.
why_flagged: State gallery supported by the Ministry of Culture, the Senate and the EU-funded National Recovery Plan. General partner Komerční banka; others include J&T Banka, Bohemia Sekt and Czech Television.
records_note: Annual reports run from 2017 to 2025 and the 2025 report names donors with amounts; no full accounts or board are posted.

name: National Gallery Singapore
funding: State funding plus corporate donors; DBS and UOB name galleries.
watch: Current patrons include casino operator Marina Bay Sands plus Bloomberg and Citadel, both on the campaign list.
why_flagged: Current patrons include casino operator Marina Bay Sands plus Bloomberg and Citadel, both on the campaign list.
records_note: The gallery posts annual reports for 2009 to 2025 with a financial report, names its patrons including Marina Bay Sands, and lists its board.

name: National Museum of American History (Smithsonian)
funding: A Smithsonian museum. About two-thirds of the Smithsonian's money comes from Congress; the rest is private gifts, endowment and earned income.
watch: In August 2025 the museum removed a reference to Trump's two impeachments from its presidency exhibit, and the White House put it under content review.
why_flagged: A Smithsonian museum. About two-thirds of the Smithsonian's money comes from Congress; the rest is private gifts, endowment and earned income.
records_note: No records of its own: parent Smithsonian posts a 2025 annual report naming donors, audited statements for 2011 to 2025, and 17 Regents.

name: National Museum of Iraq
funding: Run by Iraq's tourism and antiquities ministry. The US paid about $9M of the 2011 renovation, per its deputy director. Italy equipped its labs in 2015; France sponsored a show.
watch: In 2009 five Iraqi archaeologists wrote an open letter against a sudden reopening; the minister then removed Amira Edan as State Board of Antiquities head.
why_flagged: Run by Iraq's tourism and antiquities ministry. The US paid about $9M of the 2011 renovation, per its deputy director. Italy equipped its labs in 2015; France sponsored a show.
records_note: Its site lists no reports, accounts, donors or board, and the ministry that runs it blocked page fetches.

name: National Museum of Natural History (Smithsonian)
funding: A Smithsonian museum; Congress supplies about two-thirds of the Smithsonian's money. David H. Koch, a board member, backed the Hall of Human Origins, which carries his name.
watch: The White House named it in its August 2025 content review. In 2015, 15 groups campaigned to remove Koch from the board.
why_flagged: A Smithsonian museum; Congress supplies about two-thirds of the Smithsonian's money. David H. Koch, a board member, backed the Hall of Human Origins, which carries his name.
records_note: No records of its own: parent Smithsonian posts a 2025 annual report naming donors, audited statements for 2011 to 2025, and 17 Regents.

name: National Museum of Oman
funding: State museum set up by Royal Decree 62/2013. The Minister of Heritage and Tourism chairs its Board of Trustees.
watch: Its site describes it as a legal entity with financial and administrative independence. It shows Oman's heritage from earliest settlement to the present.
why_flagged: State museum set up by Royal Decree 62/2013. The Minister of Heritage and Tourism chairs its Board of Trustees. It lists no sponsors or budget.
records_note: It posts no reports, accounts or sponsors; its board of trustees page names six members, led by the Minister of Heritage and Tourism.

name: National Portrait Gallery
watch: Refused Sackler £1M in 2019; BP award ended 2022.
why_flagged: Refused Sackler £1M in 2019; BP award ended 2022.
records_note: It posts annual reports with audited accounts for 2012-13 to 2023-24, thanks named supporters in the latest, and lists trustees with attendance in each.

name: National Portrait Gallery (Smithsonian)
funding: A Smithsonian museum; Congress supplies about two-thirds of the Smithsonian's money, the rest from private gifts, endowment and earned income.
watch: Trump said in May 2025 he was firing director Kim Sajet, who then resigned. Amy Sherald cancelled her show in July 2025 over a painting.
why_flagged: A Smithsonian museum; Congress supplies about two-thirds of the Smithsonian's money, the rest from private gifts, endowment and earned income.
records_note: No records of its own: parent Smithsonian posts a 2025 annual report naming donors, audited statements for 2011 to 2025, and 17 Regents.
